scope: Adds a static-routing catalog lab, optional administrative-distance/explicit-interface checks on installed-route criteria, and a configured-static-route criterion for inactive floating backups. Uses the existing IOS parser and route/packet engine without adding networking commands or modifying forwarding behavior. All addressing is preconfigured. No dependency, backend or live CML validation is claimed.
verificationNotes: Network routes, host routes, defaults and floating backups are checked separately. Configuration goals stay live while actual echo observations persist. A successful ping alone cannot prove the intended route.

Fully specified primary routes bind the intended Ethernet interface and next hop, so losing the R1/R3 link withdraws the primaries. Both sides install AD 10 /24 backups through R2. This does not claim detection of a remote failure while a local interface remains up.
R1 host /32 AD 200 wins by longest-prefix match over its AD 1 default. Removing the /32 still permits default forwarding but revokes the host-route goal.
Return-path troubleshooting removes R3 LAN 20 routing, where no default can mask the missing route. R2 forward routing remains valid but PC2/server echo fails until repair.

All eight new-lab browser checks and seven general catalog checks passed, including both themes at 1440, 390 and 320 pixels and host/path/query-preserving permalinks. The frozen offline artifact and final index.html/dist/index.html match byte for byte. General catalog checks ran after the final build. No page errors or external requests were observed.
